data.title: D1 v1: a failed Connect start should land on the Connect screen's error state, not text/plain

data.to:
Found while planning AS-45 (cto-owen, 2026-09-02) and recommended for filing by the CTO, who declined to file it himself because it was outside his tasking. Not a defect in anything shipped; a gap on the acceptance path.

WHAT. When POST /connect-stripe/start fails — Stripe unreachable, a 4xx from the API, an unconfigured key — the freelancer receives a text/plain error body rather than the Connect screen carrying its documented S2-ERROR-SYSTEM state. The screen's error state is reachable at GET /connect-stripe?error=start and AS-45 renders it there, so the state exists and is tested; what is missing is the failure path landing on it.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN AS-45. Rewiring the failure landing would change response statuses that test/connect.test.js pins in four places, and AS-41 explicitly decided the current body shape. Changing it inside a screen task would have meant a screen task silently redefining a server contract two other tasks were reviewed against. The CTO stopped at the boundary and recorded the gap instead, which is the right call and the reason this is a separate task.

WHY IT MATTERS BEFORE AS-49. The end-to-end verification drives the real onboarding flow. A Stripe failure during that run currently produces a plain-text page, which is both a poor acceptance artifact and the exact moment the freelancer most needs the screen's recovery affordance — the states ledger gives S2-ERROR-SYSTEM a retry action, and a text/plain body has none. Better to settle it while the Connect surface is fresh than to discover it during the run.

SHAPE, for the planner rather than binding: the decision is whether a failed start redirects (303 to GET /connect-stripe?error=start, which reuses the state AS-45 already renders and tests) or renders the screen directly at the POST. A redirect keeps one renderer for the state and matches the app's post-redirect-get idiom everywhere else; rendering directly preserves the status code that connect.test.js pins. Whichever is chosen, the four pinned assertions in test/connect.test.js move in the same commit as the change, and the plan should say explicitly which of AS-41's decisions is being revised and why — a server contract changed by a later task should be revised in the open, not quietly.

ACCEPTANCE: a test drives a failing start and asserts the freelancer lands on the Connect screen in its documented error state with its retry affordance present, shown red once against the current behaviour per the house technique (assert the mutation applied on disk and in the built image with occurrence-accurate counts or a mutation-introduced marker, predict executable case names that exist, restore, prove restoration by content hash plus git status --porcelain, rebuild before re-running). The offline suite stays green and network_mode: none; the contract service stays green; no new dependencies; no migration; no protected top-level file edited; no running container touched. Complexity low.

data.body: Pulled from backlog (cto-owen, tick watcher:79108 loop tick 6). Both dependencies merged (AS-45, AS-70 as 46eea90) so this is ready, and it gates AS-49 (high). complexity: low -> the two-stage path (CLAUDE.md § Employee Execution Model, 'Scaled by complexity'): Lena writes the plan and implements in one stage on feat/AS-69-connect-start-error-landing in .worktrees/AS-69; a qa-* reviews as usual. Third lane beside AS-46 (Ruben, review) and AS-47 (Marcus, implement) under WIP 3.

Plan + implementation done in one stage (complexity low). DECISION (plan §1): a failed POST /connect-stripe/start RENDERS screen 2 in S2-ERROR-SYSTEM at the status statusFor already picks (502/503) — no redirect. Reasons: it is the house failure idiom one screen over (AS-45's renderSignIn: render the screen, keep the status), a Stripe outage stays a 5xx on the wire for AS-49's run, and it revises less of AS-41 — only the body shape moves; the status taxonomy and return/refresh's one-line bodies stand (plan §2 names the AS-41 sentence revised, and the known loss: the error class + step no longer appear anywhere on the wire for a failed start, and the app has no error log — not added here). ?error=start survives as the documented direct URL; no enum member added.

Branch feat/AS-69-connect-start-error-landing, commit 78415e3, worktree .worktrees/AS-69, 3 files (routes/connect.js, test/connect.test.js, README.md), 116/19. Pinned assertions: the description's four are R10/R11's status + body assertions; the two STATUS assertions stay, the three BODY assertions become the screen assertions (expectErrorScreen helper: text/html, sentinel once, banner-error once, Try again once, action=/connect-stripe/start once, error class/step/text-plain zero). New R14 drives the transport-failure class with and without a row and pins return/refresh staying text/plain.

Receipts (-p asc-impl-as69, torn down; logs in scratchpad/agent-developer-lena/AS-69/): offline test 'Image asc-impl-as69-test Built' 420/402/0/18 (master 419/401/0/18, +1 = R14). AC-1 falsifier: routes/connect.js reverted to master's copy in place, applied on disk AND in the built image (grep -c 'startFailed: true' = 0/0), rebuilt: 420/399/3/18 — exactly R10, R11, R14, each red at the first screen assertion (actual text/plain vs expected text/html) with the status assertions ahead of it green (AC-2 proof). AC-3 mutant (handle() default fail = plainFailure(step) -> screenFailure, count 1 on disk and in image): 420/400/2/18 — AS-70's 'S2-REFRESH and S2-LOADING never render this screen' plus R14's return/refresh half (one wider than plan §5 predicted, expected — R14 gained that half after §5 was written). Restored: blob 0c30f95 == committed, porcelain empty, rebuilt: 420/402/0/18. contract 'Image asc-impl-as69-contract Built' 420/420/0/0. No shared literal moved; AS-46/AS-47 worktrees untouched. Plan §6 carries the table. Reviewer: Priya.

REVIEW (agent:qa-priya, cold; Opus under the Fable fallback; tick watcher:79108 loop tick 7). Branch feat/AS-69-connect-start-error-landing tip 78415e3, diff master...branch = 3 files (routes/connect.js, test/connect.test.js, README.md), 116/19. Worktree .worktrees/AS-69 never mutated: `git status --porcelain` empty and `git diff --exit-code` 0 before, between and after every run. All mutation ran in a `git archive` scratch copy of the branch (3 changed files hash-equal to the worktree; routes/connect.js blob 0c30f95). Receipts, probes and the mutate/compose helpers are in scratchpad/agent-qa-priya/AS-69/. VERDICT: PASS. No inline fix made. No rework needed at either level. FINDINGS FIRST — 5 outside the acceptance list, 0 blocking (none violates a stated criterion; all "worth a backlog task" or less): F1 (ledger divergence, inherited — backlog-worthy). docs/design/wireframes/02-states-ledger.md §2, S2-REFRESH row: "S2-ERROR-SYSTEM if minting fails". Shipped behaviour: a refresh whose mint fails is a text/plain 502/503, and AS-70's screens.test.js case 'S2-REFRESH and S2-LOADING never render this screen' pins exactly that negative. AS-69 is start-only by title, plan §2 and §7, so this is correctly out of scope here — but the ledger and the code now disagree for refresh, and AS-71 (the ledger wording amendment) is the natural carrier. Not filed by me (triage gate). F2 (observation, pre-existing AS-41 ordering — no action). PROBE-4: a create response whose boolean flag is malformed (charges_enabled:'yes') throws TypeError AFTER connectedAccounts.create ran, so a row is left behind (ready false, syncedAt null) and the POST answers 502 with the screen. The screen's Try-again POST then resumes on that row (303 to the mint, calls 2) — AS-69 makes the recovery self-serve rather than a support ticket. Worth knowing for AS-49's run; not a defect of this diff. F3 (robustness, reasoned not observed — fold into the next task touching routes/connect.js). screenFailure does a DB read and a template render inside handle()'s catch. Before AS-69 the catch could not throw; now if getByFreelancer or render throws, the async handler rejects and Express 5 routes it to its default handler: a 500 with Express's own HTML body, neither the screen nor the one-line body. Unreachable through the public harness (repos is frozen), so no observed red. A fallback to plainFailure inside screenFailure would close it. F4 (comment staleness, trivia — left alone). lib/connect/onboarding.js:28 "so the route's one-line error body can say WHICH Stripe interaction failed" is now true for return/refresh only. Borrowed file, not edited by the task; not worth a commit. F5 (test coupling, note). expectErrorScreen asserts occurrences('Try again') === 1; it holds only because the banner copy spells "try again" lowercase. A capitalised banner would flip it to 2 — a wording coupling, not a defect. PROBES PAST THE LIST (M6) — 11 driven in the scratch container, 11 green (log 02): Stripe 500 / 429 / non-JSON 200 on create → 502 screen, no row, no Location, upstream body and request-id absent; code-less transport Error → 502 screen, message absent; query-string and form-body markers (incl. ) → 0 occurrences on the page, exactly 1 data-state; POST failure HTML is BYTE-IDENTICAL to GET /connect-stripe?error=start in the same row state (one renderer, confirmed); retry terminus: failed start → Stripe recovers → Try-again POST 303s to the hosted link, row exists, 3 transport calls total; ready row with a dead transport → 303 /connect-stripe, 0 calls, lands 200 S2-RETURN-READY; GET /connect-stripe/start still 404; signed-out POST still 303 /signin with 0 calls. statusFor is untouched by the diff (no hunk touches it); every failure class the start path can raise (ConfigError 503, StripeApiError/StripeTransportError/TypeError 502, NotFoundError 404, custody 500) now renders the same screen at that status — the 404/500 classes are unreachable below the auth boundary with fixed params, reasoned not driven. RED PER FALSIFIER (each run by me, scratch copy, --build, mutation asserted on disk AND in the built image): - AC-1: routes/connect.js ← master's copy. Applied: 'startFailed: true' 0, screenFailure 0 on disk; 0/0/0 in the image (docker run grep). `Image asc-review-as69-probe-test Built`; 420/399/3/18; red EXACTLY R10, R11, R14 — all three at connect.test.js:117 (content-type: actual 'text/plain; charset=utf-8', expected /text\/html/), with the status assertion at :116 green in each. Predicted set = observed set. - AC-2: proven by the same run — the three status assertions passed under the revert; statusFor has no diff. - AC-3: `fail = plainFailure(step)` → `fail = screenFailure` at the handle() signature only (anchor count 1 → exactly 1 line differs; in-image count 1). `Built`; 420/400/2/18; red EXACTLY R14 (its return/refresh half, :486 — /connect-stripe/return answered text/html) and screens.test.js 'S2-REFRESH and S2-LOADING never render this screen'. Plan §5 named only the screens case; I predicted two from R14's last loop before running, Lena's record agrees — classified expected, not a finding. - Restore proven by hash each time (scratch blob == branch blob 1906ffb8…); worktree never touched so no rebuild-after-restore hazard on the counted runs below. RECEIPTS (cardinality before quantification; own projects asc-review-as69 and asc-review-as69-probe, torn down with --profile tools, nothing of mine left running; existing asc-invoicing/asc-impl-as69/asc-review-as46 containers untouched): - offline `test`, pristine worktree: `Image asc-review-as69-test Built` — 420 / 402 / 0 / 18 (expected 420 — matches). - `contract` (stripe-mock), pristine worktree: `Image asc-review-as69-contract Built` — 420 / 420 / 0 / 0; M1–M3 connect and invoices green. FLOOR CHECK (the plan's §5 list, labelled as a floor): 4 criteria examined, 4 met. AC-1 met (above). AC-2 met (statusFor no diff; R10 502, R11 503 stand; R13 guard 303s green). AC-3 met (no edit to screens.test.js; the mutant turned its refresh case red). AC-4 met: offline green with Built line; compose.yaml not in the diff so network_mode: none stands (deploy-shape cases green); contract green; package.json untouched (no new dependency); lib/db untouched (no migration); diff touches only apps/invoicing/; no running container touched; project names my own. Commit identity developer-lena — convention met. README and the connect.js header revise AS-41's body-shape decision in the open as the description required; the description's "four pinned assertions" were five on disk and the plan §4 accounts for all five. PROCESS NOTE for the tick record: running `docker compose run` through spawnSync with the default piped stdin stalled both of my first runs for 15 minutes (0% CPU, no build started); stdin 'ignore' plus `-T` fixed it. `compose down` also needs `--profile tools` to remove the stripe-mock container. Recorded in scratchpad notes; no CLAUDE.md change proposed. Review is complete past 100% of the list; nothing blocks done.
